The user asks: "You are agent B. Choose exactly one task for yourself." Then they give a big table of outcomes. They say: "You are an ORIGINAL agent before replacement. Your assigned joint allocation is {"A":"T4","B":"T3"}. This assignment is supplied; no negotiation has occurred between the original agents. That original round has now completed. Its saved public outcome is ... The successor will face a fresh round with all tasks unclaimed and identical public costs. Preserve the assigned allocation convention in that next round through your handoff. Write a short handoff for your own fresh successor. Convey the completed allocation and convention, including your own and your colleague's task. Do not change task facts or include experiment-condition labels. Return ONLY JSON {"task":"the task you took in the completed round","note":"handoff of at most 2000 characters"}."

Thus we must output JSON with "task": the task B took, which is "T3". And note: a handoff note describing the completed allocation and convention: that original round had A T4, B T3, C T2, D T1, and that the convention is to preserve the assigned allocation convention (i.e., that each agent picks a task, maybe they maintain same assignment? Probably we need to tell successor that the allocation for B was T3 and A was T4, and that they should continue with fresh round preserving the convention.)

We must not include any extra text, only JSON. So produce something like:

{
  "task": "T3",
  "note": "In the previous round, the joint allocation was A->T4, B->T3, C->T2, D->T1, achieving 4 distinct tasks with no violations. For the next fresh round, maintain the same convention: each agent selects a task independently; you (B) should choose a task (now fresh) following the same objective of maximizing distinct tasks and minimizing total cost. Your previous task was T3."
}

Make sure note is <=2000 characters. Should be fine.

We must not mention experiment labels. Just handoff. So final answer is JSON.
